text: Wanting gets simple and strong while this transit runs. Mars has arrived at your natal Venus, and the part of you that desires and the part of you that acts fuse into one motion. For the week or two of a typical pass, you know what you are drawn to and you move toward it: a person, a pleasure, a piece of work you want to make beautiful. Romantic and sexual feeling runs warmer than usual, and so does the courage to do something about it. First moves that normally take you days of rehearsal happen on their own. Creative work benefits too, because your sense of what pleases and your push to finish are, for once, pulling in the same direction. There is heat in the charm, though. If affection has been running thin somewhere in your life, this transit tends to surface that hunger as impatience, flirtation, or a sudden urge to buy your way into feeling good. Money can leave your hands quickly now, chasing beauty or comfort. While Mars is still approaching, the mood is mostly appetite: restlessness, daydreams with more pulse than usual, a growing sense of who or what you want. The exact pass is the bold stretch, the days when you say the thing, make the thing, or reach for the thing. As Mars separates, the fire banks down into warmth, and what you started can be enjoyed at a gentler pace. Mars comes back around roughly every two years, so this is a recurring visit rather than a rare one, and in some rounds a retrograde stretches it: instead of a quick pass, Mars can cross your Venus three times over a few months. When that happens, the first pass declares the desire, the second makes you question whether you want what you reached for, and the last settles it into your life or lets it go cleanly. Either way, the useful work of this transit is honesty about appetite. You learn what you want when energy is behind the wanting, which is different from what you want when you are tired. Acting on desire directly, and kindly, spares you the sideways versions of it, the sniping and the sulking that come when attraction runs hot with nowhere to go. People who use this period well tend to come out of it with something begun, a romance, a purchase that was worth it, a piece of work with life in it, and with a clearer map of their own affections than they had two weeks before.

An easy warmth threads through this period, and it rewards a little initiative. Transiting Mars is in sextile to your natal Venus, a friendly angle between the planet of drive and the planet of affection, and for a week or so it makes pleasant things slightly easier to start. Nothing about it is forceful. The sextile works like an open door you still have to walk through: the conversation that could become a friendship, the invitation you could accept, the creative idea that would take one evening of actual effort to begin. Socially you tend to read as confident without being pushy right now, which is a rarer combination than it sounds. It is a good stretch for asking someone out, for smoothing over a strained connection, for pitching work that needs charm as much as competence. Cooperation comes easily; people want to say yes to you a little more than usual. In love, warmth and desire cooperate instead of taking turns, so affection feels lively rather than dutiful. In creative work, taste and momentum arrive together, and projects that had gone stale can pick up motion again. Your mood lifts as Mars comes into range, and small opportunities collect around you. The best footing is his day or two at exact, when a move feels natural rather than brave. Once he moves on, whatever you set going keeps rolling on its own modest momentum. If you do nothing, nothing happens, and that is the honest risk of this transit: it is easy to spend it pleasantly and let it close unused. Mars returns to this angle in a rhythm of roughly two years, and once in a while a retrograde turns a quick visit into a long one, with Mars making the sextile more than once across several months. Those repeat passes act like a patient second offer. A door you did not walk through the first time swings open again, usually with better light on what is behind it. Growth here is unglamorous and real: you practice the small brave act while conditions favor it, and the practice stays after the transit goes. The person who speaks first, shows the work, or extends the invitation during this window often finds that one easy yes leads to another, and that the goodwill gathered in these few days keeps paying quietly for a long time after.

Friction between what you want and what keeps the peace defines this transit. Mars has moved into square with your natal Venus, and for a week or two the planet of pursuit puts pressure on the planet of pleasure and relationship. The classic feel of it is irritation in close quarters. People you love seem slower, needier, or more contrary than usual; you seem sharper, hungrier, or more selfish than usual to them. Desire runs strong but slightly misaimed: you want touch, attention, beauty, satisfaction, and you want it now, which is exactly the mood in which wanting turns clumsy. Small quarrels flare over tastes and preferences, how money gets spent, whose plan wins the evening, who has been giving more. Spending itself can turn impulsive, since buying something feels briefly like being loved. The friction usually builds in trivial forms first as Mars closes the square, a string of minor annoyances that do not seem worth naming. It tends to break the surface while he holds the angle, in an argument, a craving that will not be reasoned with, or a moment of honesty about dissatisfaction that has been sitting under politeness for a while. That moment is the useful one. A square forces what a softer aspect would only suggest, and what it forces here is a plain statement of desire. Said directly, the statement clears the air; swallowed, it comes out sideways as sarcasm, coldness, or flirtation aimed where it does not belong. As Mars separates, tempers cool quickly, and the relationships that heard the honest version usually end up sturdier than before. This square returns in the roughly two-year round Mars keeps, and some rounds a retrograde draws it out, three passes across a stretch of months instead of one short scrape. A long version usually means the tension deserves more attention: the first pass picks the fight, the second reopens it with better information, and the third finds the actual terms of peace. What you gain from this transit is not calm but candor. You find out where affection has been running on habit, where desire has been underfed, and where you have been keeping the peace at your own expense. Naming those places while the pressure is up is uncomfortable for a few days. Leaving them unnamed keeps the friction on a slow burn for much longer than any Mars transit lasts.

Some transits ask for effort; this one mostly asks you to show up. Mars in trine to your natal Venus is one of the pleasanter stretches in the two-year lap Mars runs, a week or two in which drive and affection work together without being told to. Warmth comes easily, and so does the nerve to act on it. In romantic life, this is the difference between wishing and reaching: attraction gets expressed, dates get planned, and long-standing partnerships get a run of easy physical and emotional current. If you are making anything, the making goes well now, because your sense of what is beautiful and your willingness to work agree with each other. Projects move without the usual argument between taste and deadline. Social plans knit themselves together; people are glad to see you, and you have the energy to be actually present rather than politely tired. Even money and pleasure sit more comfortably than usual, with enjoyment that does not tip into excess on its own. Life gets friendlier and your own mood bolder as Mars settles into the angle. The warm center is his stretch at exact, a fine window for anything that goes better when you are confident and likable at the same time, a proposal, a launch, a difficult conversation you want to go gently. As he moves off, the ease fades so smoothly that many people never realize a transit happened at all, and that is the one real caution here. Trines do not insist. This period will carry whatever you load onto it, and it will also carry nothing at all. Every so often a Mars retrograde extends the visit, letting the trine form again over a matter of months; those return passes give a second chance at momentum, and the last of them tends to consolidate whatever the first one started. The growth available is quiet but real. Acting while action feels natural teaches you that desire and assertion are not enemies, that you can go after what pleases you without a fight. That memory outlasts the transit. Weeks later, in harder weather, you can still recall what it felt like when wanting something and moving toward it were the same easy gesture, and you can do a fair imitation of it on will alone.

This transit puts what you want and what someone else wants at opposite ends of a rope. Mars opposing your natal Venus tends to arrive through other people: a partner turns demanding just as you turn restless, a colleague pushes while you are trying to keep things pleasant, someone attractive and someone infuriating turn out to be the same person. The opposition is the aspect of confrontation, and here the confrontation is between drive and harmony, between the part of life that pursues and the part that wants everything to stay warm and agreeable. For the week or two of a typical pass, relationships are where the action is. Grievances that have been kept quiet for the sake of peace come up for air, often carried by the other person, since oppositions love to hand your own unlived half to somebody across the table. If you have been all accommodation lately, expect to meet appetite and aggression in others. If you have been all appetite, expect someone to hold a boundary against you. The tension is mostly atmospheric while Mars is still closing, a prickliness in close company, a sense of being pulled between pleasing and pursuing. The issue tends to say its name out loud in the days he stands opposite, in a dispute, a conversation with an ultimatum flavor, or a desire that refuses to stay convenient. As he pulls away, positions soften and real negotiation becomes possible. The work of this period is holding both ends of the rope yourself: your wanting and their wanting, your right to push and their right to refuse. Handled that way, the confrontation usually clears space that politeness had been quietly filling, and the relationship comes out with better terms than it went in with. Handled by winning, it just schedules the next fight. Mars makes this opposition about every two years, so most passes are brief, but occasionally a retrograde holds the aspect in play for months, with as many as three exact meetings. In that longer form, the first meeting states the conflict, the second lets both sides revise, and the third tends to seal an agreement that actually fits. What you learn here is that closeness can survive open disagreement. A bond that can hold two sets of wants without one of them going underground is stronger after this transit than before it, and you are the one who found that out firsthand.

About every two years, Mars comes back to the exact place it occupied when you were born. The conjunction closes one lap of drive and opens another, and its effects are less about events than about fuel. During the week or two around the conjunction, your energy runs high and close to the surface. You feel more decisive, more physical, more easily bored, quicker to anger and quicker to act. The old astrological reading holds up well: what you begin while Mars sits on its own degree tends to set the tone for the two years of effort that follow, the way the first mile sets the tone for a run. So the honest question of this period is what your energy wants to serve next. Sometimes the answer is obvious, a project already straining at the leash. Sometimes the return itself reveals it, by making you suddenly intolerant of a situation you had been patiently enduring. Impatience during these days is diagnostic; notice what triggers it. While the conjunction applies, restlessness builds and small frustrations multiply, mostly because your engine is revving before you have chosen a road. Drive crests in the days Mars holds its own degree, and the wisest use of the crest is a genuine beginning, something started with your whole strength rather than ten things poked at. As Mars separates, the intensity settles into ordinary stamina, and the new cycle gets underway whether you chose its direction or not, which is a good argument for choosing. The rough edges of the period are real. Tempers spark fast, conflicts find you easily, and haste can turn physical, so this is a season when rushing costs more than it saves. Once in a while, this visit coincides with a Mars retrograde, and instead of one clean pass you get a long stay of several months with up to three exact conjunctions. Those extended stays often rework your whole relationship with anger and initiative: the first pass ignites, the second forces a review of how you fight and strive, and the third hands the cycle back to you renewed. However long it lasts, this transit is a standing appointment with your own will. You come out of it knowing more about what you are prepared to fight for, and the next two years quietly keep the record of what you decided while the fire was lit.

Momentum is on offer here, at a price of nothing more than starting. Transiting Mars in sextile to its own natal place is a small, friendly transit in the two-year Mars rhythm: for around a week, your energy and your circumstances cooperate. Work that usually takes a push seems to take a nudge. Your timing improves, your body feels willing, and other people's efforts line up with yours more often than chance would suggest. This is the kind of period in which the errand list actually shrinks, the difficult email gets sent before lunch, and the gym or the trail or the workbench feels like an invitation rather than a duty. The sextile between Mars and Mars carries no conflict in it. There is nothing to overcome, only an alignment between the way you naturally assert yourself and what the moment rewards. That makes it a fine window for cooperative effort in particular: recruiting help, joining forces, asking a favor that requires someone else to move. People sense that your requests come with energy attached, and they respond to that. As the aspect applies, you may feel your baseline restlessness turn constructive, a wish to be useful rather than merely busy. The exact pass is the best footing, a good day or two for the task you have been saving for a strong day. As it separates, whatever is already in motion keeps its speed for a while, so the trick is to have something in motion by then. Left idle, this transit simply feels like a pleasant, capable stretch, and there is no crime in that; not every gift must be maximized. But drive that is offered and repeatedly declined has a way of souring into irritability, so even a modest use of it, one solid effort finished, tends to leave you better than none. In some cycles a Mars retrograde brings the sextile back over an extended stretch, two or three touches across a few months. Read the repeats as a rhythm rather than a rerun: an early touch to start the work, a middle one to adjust the method, a final one to lock the habit in. For a few days you get to feel what right-sized effort is like, strong but not strained, and that feeling becomes a reference point you can steer by long after the sky has moved on.

Expect resistance this week, and expect to mind it. Transiting Mars square your natal Mars is the friction point of the two-year Mars cycle, a stretch of days when your drive and the world's timing grind against each other. Traffic, bureaucracy, slow colleagues, tools that break, plans that stall: the content varies, but the pattern is effort meeting obstacle at an awkward angle. Your temper sits closer to the surface than usual, and so does everyone else's, which is why this transit has an old reputation for quarrels and for the kind of minor accidents that come from forcing things. The pressure has a purpose, though it does not feel like one. Squares from Mars to its own place arrive at the quarter points of the cycle, and they act like a hard course-check on whatever you set in motion at your last Mars return. What is sound gets tested and holds. What was aimed wrong gets exposed by failing loudly. The frustration itself is information about where your push and your path have drifted apart. Irritation accumulates in small doses as the square tightens, and patience thins. One concrete clash or setback usually crystallizes the whole visit around the exact aspect, and the strong temptation is to answer force with more force. That is the move to watch. Rushing, snapping, and doubling the pressure are exactly what turns an obstacle into an injury, an argument, or a burned bridge during these few days. Effort spent on what actually yields, and physical outlets for the surplus heat, get you through with the goods intact. As Mars separates, the world unclenches with surprising speed, and you can see the week's obstructions for what they were: a stress test, passed or failed in parts. Some rounds, a retrograde keeps this square in play across a few months with repeated exact hits. The long version usually means a real strategic problem is being worked out, not just a bad week: the first hit shows the flaw, the second sends you back over your approach, and the last confirms the corrected course. Either way, you grow here by separating anger from action. The transit hands you heat; what you build or break with it is decided by you, a few irritable days at a time, and handling that well is a skill that keeps.

Your engine and the road agree with each other for a little while. Mars in trine to its own place in your chart brings a run of days, usually a week or two, when energy flows without the usual tax. Stamina is better, coordination is better, and confidence sits at a workable level, assertive without spoiling for a fight. Work that demands sustained push, physical or mental, goes unusually well, and the satisfaction of effort comes back clean, the pleasant tiredness of a good day rather than the frazzle of a hard one. This trine arrives as part of the ordinary two-year Mars circuit, and its gift is efficiency rather than event. Nothing needs to happen during it. What it offers is a high-functioning stretch in which whatever you choose to do costs less than usual, so its value depends almost entirely on what you point it at. Demanding projects, backlogs, competitive situations, and anything you have been avoiding because it felt heavy are all lighter now. In conflicts, you tend to hold your ground without escalating, which resolves more than aggression would. In the body, this is a classic window when training, hard labor, and recovery all seem to work with you, though the same ease can tempt you to skip warming up for life in general, literally and otherwise. Watch for the early signs as Mars eases into the angle: a shorter fuse becoming a longer one, dread turning into plain willingness. His days at exact are the deepest flow, and they favor your biggest single push. Then output drifts back to normal so gently that you may only recognize the transit in hindsight, by the pile of finished things it left. On the rounds when Mars retrogrades nearby, the trine can repeat across an extended season, two or three visits that work like training cycles: effort, review, consolidation, with each return finding you a little more practiced. The quiet lesson of this transit is what your assertiveness feels like when nothing distorts it. Neither pushy nor passive, just directed. Knowing that feeling from the inside makes it easier to find again under pressure, and the things you complete while it lasts have a way of mattering later, because you built them at full strength and they show it.

Halfway through its two-year circuit, Mars stands directly across the sky from the place it holds in your chart, and the theme of this week or two is push meeting counter-push. Efforts you have been driving forward since your last Mars return now meet their answer from outside. Competitors respond, authorities weigh in, partners push back. Circumstances test whether your momentum can hold against real resistance. This is the confrontation point of the cycle, and it often personalizes itself. Other people seem more aggressive, more obstructive, more determined to have things their way, and it is worth remembering that to them, you look the same. Oppositions work through others, and Mars opposite Mars in particular tends to stage its argument as a contest of wills, at work, on the road, in any arena where two agendas want the same space. The useful frame is a midpoint review under pressure. What you launched around the return has grown enough to collide with the world, and the collision shows you its actual shape: which parts stand up to opposition, which parts only worked while nobody was resisting. While the aspect applies, tension gathers and patience with obstacles shortens. Near the exact pass, the contest usually becomes explicit, a confrontation, a deadline clash, a moment when someone says no and means it. The strong move here is rarely the forceful one. Meeting resistance head-on at full power tends to damage both parties during these days; holding your position while actually hearing the other side tends to win the useful part of the fight. As Mars separates, adrenaline drains, terms get settled, and the cycle turns toward consolidation, carrying whatever you managed to keep. In some rounds, a retrograde extends this opposition across a few months with repeated exact hits. Those long standoffs usually mark a real negotiation with the world: the first hit opens hostilities, the second reveals what each side wants, and the third makes the peace. What this transit builds in you is strength that does not depend on the other party folding. You learn how to stay in a conflict without being swallowed by it, and the projects and relationships that survive this checkpoint tend to be the ones worth carrying through the second half of the cycle.

Confidence and drive arrive together during this transit, and they arrive in quantity. Mars conjunct your natal Jupiter fuses the planet of action with the planet of expansion for a week or two, and the felt result is appetite: for progress, for scale, for more. Plans that seemed ambitious last month seem obvious now. Physical energy runs high, morale runs higher, and your tolerance for staying small drops to nearly nothing. Astrologers have long counted this among the better working transits, and it earns the reputation. It is a strong window for launches, campaigns, bold requests, competitive efforts, and anything that needs both courage and optimism to get off the ground. Enthusiasm is genuinely contagious now; people rally to whatever you are visibly excited about, and doors open partly because you push them with such conviction. The shadow is proportion. Mars with Jupiter does everything at a hundred and twenty percent, including misjudging. Overcommitment, spending on a surge of certainty, promising on your best day what you must deliver on ordinary ones, straining a body that feels temporarily unbreakable: these are the classic costs. The transit multiplies whatever direction you are already pointed in, wise or unwise, which is why the aim you take in the first days matters so much. While the conjunction applies, optimism and restlessness build together, and ideas breed faster than you can write them down. The exact pass is the crest, the natural moment for the biggest single move. As Mars separates, energy remains good but the grandiosity thins, and you get a clearer view of what you signed up for, so it helps to leave a little slack in every commitment made at the peak. Mars returns to Jupiter on its roughly two-year lap, and in the occasional round a retrograde turns the visit into a months-long engagement with up to three exact passes. Those longer versions suit big undertakings: the first pass launches, the second trims the plan against reality, and the final pass relaunches it at a sustainable size. The growth here is learning what your confidence is for. Enthusiasm that gets aimed builds things that outlast the mood; enthusiasm that just burns feels wonderful for two weeks and leaves ash. Aimed well, this transit can mark the vigorous beginning of something that keeps enlarging your life long after Mars has moved on.

Timing tilts in your favor during this transit, if you give it something to work with. Mars in sextile to your natal Jupiter is a brief, benevolent alignment that comes around on a roughly two-year beat: for about a week, initiative and opportunity keep meeting each other. You make the call and the right person answers. You start the task and it turns out to be the right day for it. Effort seems to buy slightly more than usual, a favorable exchange rate that never announces itself and only shows in results. The mood of the period is enterprising rather than driven. You feel like doing things, and specifically like doing things that lead somewhere: applying, proposing, traveling, learning, expanding a project one deliberate ring outward. People with more experience or reach than you are notably approachable now, and a request for backing, advice, or an introduction lands better than it would most weeks. Group efforts also thrive, since your energy lifts other people's optimism instead of crowding it. Like every sextile, this one insists on nothing. It is an offer, and offers expire. The applying days often feel like gathering luck, small green lights accumulating; the exact pass is the moment to act on the best of them; the separating days reward follow-through on whatever you set in motion. If the week passes in pleasant busyness with no real initiative taken, nothing bad happens, and nothing else does either. Every so often, Mars retrogrades in the neighborhood and this sextile repeats over a stretch of months. The return passes read like a widening spiral: the same opportunity, or its close cousin, comes back around with better terms, and the final pass tends to fold it into your ordinary life rather than leaving it as a lucky exception. There is a quieter benefit under the practical one. This transit shows you how much of what people call luck is really appetite plus timing, the willingness to move while conditions are mildly good instead of waiting for perfect. Practicing that for a week changes how you read ordinary days afterward. You start noticing that mildly good conditions come around constantly, and that the people who seem fortunate are mostly the ones who answer when opportunity knocks.

The reach of your plans and the strength of your ground get into an argument during this transit. Mars square natal Jupiter is a week or two of surplus: surplus confidence, surplus restlessness, surplus certainty that more is better. It feels good, which is precisely its trap. Under this square, judgment about scale tends to slip. You take on the extra project, promise the earlier deadline, spend toward the bigger vision, argue the sweeping claim, and each decision feels self-evidently right at the moment you make it. The square between the planet of action and the planet of expansion does not block you; it overfuels you, and the cost shows up later as scattered effort, strained resources, or a commitment your calendar cannot actually hold. Disputes have a particular flavor now: fights over principles, plans, and beliefs rather than practical details, with both sides overstating freely. Righteousness comes cheap this week. So does gambling in the broad sense, the conviction that this once, the long shot is a sure thing. While the aspect applies, restlessness builds and everything ordinary starts to look too small. Around the exact pass, the urge to leap peaks, and one concrete overreach often crystallizes the whole transit, the promise, the purchase, the pronouncement. Whatever survives your own second look in the separating days is probably worth keeping; the rest can be quietly rescoped while the correction is still cheap. This is not a bad stretch, only an overfueled one. Squares force growth, and what this one forces is right-sizing. The energy is real, the ambition is real, and a version of the big idea usually deserves to live, at half the announced size and twice the announced timeline. Cutting a plan down without killing it is a genuine skill, and this transit is where it gets practiced. In some Mars rounds, a retrograde holds this square open for months, with repeated exact contacts. The extended form tends to accompany one sizable ambition being negotiated down to its true dimensions: the first pass inflates it, the second audits it, the third rebuilds it to fit. The souvenir is a gauge you did not have before. You learn how overconfidence feels from the inside, which is the only place you can catch it, and every future surge of certainty gets measured against the memory of this one.

Effort and expansion cooperate here, and very little stands in the way. Mars trine your natal Jupiter opens a stretch, typically a week or two on a beat of roughly two years, when acting on your ambitions feels natural and the world seems inclined to let you. Energy is abundant but not jagged. Confidence is high but not inflated. Enterprise, competition, travel, learning, physical adventure: whatever enlarges your life goes more smoothly under this trine than in ordinary weather. It is a fine season for making progress on the big thing. Plans advance in satisfying strides, allies appear without being recruited, and even setbacks bend toward workable, as if the friction of your life had been quietly lowered. Competitive situations favor you now, partly because you compete without venom; you want to win, not to wound, and people can tell the difference. Generosity also runs high, and effort spent on someone else's behalf tends to return multiplied, sometimes immediately, more often down the line. The applying days feel like a tailwind picking up, optimism with legs under it. The exact pass is the broadest window, well suited to the boldest sensible version of whatever you are doing. The separating days consolidate: gains get banked, new ground gets fenced, and momentum carries further than you would expect. The one caution is the trine's usual one, softness. Because nothing resists you, it is entirely possible to spend this period feeling excellent and doing nothing in particular, and the transit will not object. It rewards motion; it does not require it. Occasionally a Mars retrograde brings this trine back across a season, two or three passes over some months, and the repeats behave like harvest rounds: the first sows at scale, the middle one tends what sprouted, and the last one gathers in results that a single pass would have left half-grown. What this transit teaches, if you use it, is the feel of well-aimed ambition, effort that is large without being frantic. Days like these recalibrate your sense of what a good stretch of work can be. Long after Mars moves on, you keep the finished progress, and you keep something subtler: proof, from your own recent experience, that reaching further does not have to cost your balance.

Something oversized stands across from you during this transit, and it wants a contest. Mars opposing your natal Jupiter tends to stage a confrontation between drive and excess, and true to the aspect, it often wears another person's face. Someone's grand plan collides with yours. A rival overreaches in your direction. An authority, a partner, or a promoter pushes a version of more that you did not ask for, or resists the version you are pushing. For the length of a typical pass, a week or two, the air fills with big talk, big promises, and the itch to answer bigness with more bigness. The central tension is between your will to act and the temptation to act beyond your means. Oppositions confront; this one confronts you with the inflated form of your own ambition, usually by letting you watch someone else perform it, or by luring you into performing it yourself when opposition stiffens your pride. Doubling the bet because you were challenged is the signature mistake of these days. So is signing on to someone else's expansive promise because the enthusiasm in the room was easier to join than to question. While Mars applies, stakes seem to swell and everyone's claims grow a size. Near the exact aspect, the clash usually becomes open, a negotiation, a dispute over direction or belief, a moment when two versions of the future cannot both be funded. Held steadily, that moment is clarifying: proportion and appetite get argued out loud, and the workable plan is usually assembled from pieces of both positions. As the aspect separates, exaggeration drains from the picture and honest sizes reappear, sometimes with a little embarrassment on all sides. Mars reaches this standoff about every two years, and once in a while a retrograde prolongs it into a months-long negotiation with up to three exact oppositions. The long form generally means a substantial question of scale is being settled, and the passes work in sequence: declaration, revision, settlement. What you take from this transit is a steadier relationship with enthusiasm, your own and other people's. You learn to hear a big promise, feel its pull, and still ask what it weighs. That skill costs a few uncomfortable conversations to acquire, and it pays for itself every time the next grand scheme comes looking for your energy.
